LearningOutcomes: Students will be able to define economics, distinguish between microeconomics and macroeconomics, explain the concepts of scarcity and opportunity cost, and describe Kenya's key economic sectors.
LectureTopics: What is Economics? Microeconomics vs Macroeconomics
Scarcity, choice, and opportunity cost in the Kenyan economy
The circular flow of income in a modern open economy
Overview of Kenya's economic structure: agriculture, services, and the digital economy

Materials.Title: Introduction to Business Economics - Lecture Slides

AssessmentMethods: In-class discussion, reflective journal entry, weekly quiz
FeedbackComments: Well-structured introduction with excellent use of local Kenyan economic data. Students engaged well with the discussion on the digital economy.

LearningOutcomes: Students will be able to analyse supply and demand curves, determine market equilibrium, calculate price elasticity, and apply these concepts to real Kenyan market scenarios.
LectureTopics: The law of demand: factors affecting consumer behaviour in Kenya
The law of supply: production costs, market incentives, and supply shifters
Market equilibrium and price determination mechanisms
Price elasticity of demand and supply with Kenyan market examples

Materials.Title: Supply and Demand Analysis - Lecture Slides
Supply and Demand: Lecture Notes and Worked Examples

AssessmentMethods: Problem-solving exercises, group case study analysis on Nairobi market dynamics
FeedbackComments: Excellent use of local market examples. The case study on Nairobi food prices was particularly effective in contextualising demand theory.

Topic: Introduction to Database Systems and ER Modelling

LectureTopics: Evolution of data management: from file systems to relational database systems
Advantages of DBMS over file-based systems and the three-schema architecture
Entity-Relationship modelling: entities, attributes, and relationship types
Drawing ER diagrams: cardinality, participation constraints, and weak entities

Materials.Title: Introduction to Database Systems - Lecture Slides
ER Modelling: Notes and Worked Examples
Lab Exercise: Design an ER Diagram for a Student Registration System

AssessmentMethods: Lab exercise: ER diagram design, short quiz on DBMS concepts and terminology
FeedbackComments: Well-organised introduction to database systems. The ER diagram lab exercise is practical and directly relevant to the course project.

LearningOutcomes: Students will be able to identify and explain the primary sources of law in Kenya, describe the hierarchy of courts, explain the doctrine of precedent, and analyse the role of the Constitution as the supreme law of Kenya.
LectureTopics: Overview of the Kenyan legal system and its historical development
The Constitution of Kenya 2010 as the supreme law: key provisions and principles
Legislation, delegated legislation, and the legislative process in Kenya
Case law, customary law, and the role of international law in Kenya's legal framework

Materials.Title: Sources of Law in Kenya - Lecture Slides
The Constitution of Kenya 2010 - Selected Provisions

AssessmentMethods: Case law reading and discussion, take-home reflection on constitutional rights and the Bill of Rights
FeedbackComments: Excellent grounding in Kenyan law. The use of the 2010 Constitution as a central reference point is well-judged for first-year students.

LearningOutcomes: Students will be able to describe the phases of the SDLC, compare waterfall and agile methodologies, explain Scrum roles and ceremonies, and evaluate the suitability of different SDLC models for given project scenarios.
LectureTopics: Introduction to software engineering: principles, importance, and career landscape in Kenya
Phases of the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC): from requirements to maintenance
Waterfall vs Agile methodologies: comparison, advantages, and trade-offs
Introduction to Scrum: roles, sprints, ceremonies, and artefacts in Agile development

Assignment: Agile vs Waterfall - Select a Methodology for a Given Project

Offer and acceptance: rules, communication, and their application in modern e-commerce
Consideration: definition, types, rules, and the doctrine of privity of contract
Capacity to contract and intention to create legal relations in Kenya
